english.title: Cause / permit the destruction / falsification of information / material relating to information / assessment notice
english.standardoffencewording:

(A)_[information notice requiring you to provide the Commissioner with information]_
(B)_[assessment notice requiring you to direct the Commissioner to material]_
(C)_[assessment notice requiring you to assist the Commissioner to view information]_

(F)_[blocking]_

english.legislation: Contrary to section 148(2)(b) and 196(2) of the Data Protection Act 2018.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
having been given an information notice / assessment notice
caused or permitted the destruction/ disposal / concealment / blocking / falsification of information or material
with the intention of preventing the Commissioner from viewing /being provided with / being directed to
all or part of that information / material

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Prosecution only by the Commissioner or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.
(ii) It is a defence for a person charged with an offence under section 148(3) to prove that the destruction, disposal, concealment, blocking or falsification would have occurred in the absence of the person being given the notice.
(iii) Where this offence has been committed by a body corporate, and it is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of or to be attributable to neglect on the part of a director, manager, secretary or similar officer of the body corporate, or a person who was purporting to act in such a capacity, the director, manager, secretary, as well as the body corporate is guilty of the offence and proceedings can also be taken against them.
(iv) Section 199(1) of the Data Protection Act 2018 states that the National Police Records (Recordable Offences) Regulations 2000 (S.I. 2000/1139) has effect as if this offence was listed in the Schedule to the Regulations. Therefore offenders must be fingerprinted and photographed as well as the offence being PNC recordable.
